_about: The federal layer of lexflow.benefits as official pointers: each program's administering agency, its official page (with a quote lexflow's fetch matched on it) and the law that creates it (a citation only: this copy has no index of the United States Code, so the law is not quoted). Federal, and applies in every state; not modelled in depth.

programs.name: Social Security retirement benefits
programs.law: Social Security Act, Title II (42 U.S.C. § 402)
programs.note: Most jobs are covered; some state and local government jobs are not covered by Social Security (the employer and the system's handbook say which).

source.quote: You can typically get monthly Retirement benefits starting at age 62 if you've worked and paid Social Security taxes for 10 years or more.

appeal.text: Ask the Social Security Administration to review a decision you disagree with.

source.quote: Request that an application decision be reviewed.

programs.name: Social Security survivors benefits
programs.law: Social Security Act, Title II (42 U.S.C. § 402)

source.quote: You might qualify for Family or Survivor benefits based on a family member’s work. These benefits could start before age 62.

appeal.text: Ask the Social Security Administration to review a decision you disagree with.

source.quote: Request that an application decision be reviewed.

programs.name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
programs.law: Social Security Act, Title XVI (42 U.S.C. § 1381 et seq.)
programs.note: Means-tested: for people 65 or older, blind or disabled, with little income and few resources.

source.quote: SSI provides monthly payments to people with disabilities and older adults who have little or no income or resources.
VA pension benefits are available to some wartime Veterans and their survivors—find out if you’re eligible to apply.

A VA Survivors Pension offers monthly payments to qualified surviving spouses and unmarried dependent children of wartime Veterans who meet certain income and net worth limits set by Congress.
